'''Valeria Francisca Eugenia Leopoldina de María de Guadalupe Souza Saldívar''' is a Mexican scientist who specializes in evolutionary and microbial ecology. She is a senior researcher in the Department of Evolutionary Ecology of the Institute of Ecology of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] and a level III researcher in the National System of Researchers.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Padilla|first=Greta|date=2019-10-16|title=Valeria Souza Saldívar, la primera mujer mexicana reconocida por la Academia Americana de Artes y Ciencias|url=https://www.sopitas.com/noticias/valeria-souza-saldivar-primera-mexicana-reconocida-academia-americana-artes-ciencias/|access-date=2021-03-09|website=Sopitas}}</ref> She was the former president of the Scientific Society of Ecology of Mexico.

== Early education and career==
Souza was born in Mexico City in 1958.<ref name=":8" /> Her father, Antonio Souza, was an art collector and critic who first discovered, in 1960, the painter [[Francisco Toledo]].<ref name=":8" /> As an eight year old, she decided she wanted to become a biologist.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gómez Duran|first=Thelma|date=2019-11-08|title=Valeria Souza: la científica mexicana que estudia los microorganismos más antiguos del planeta|url=https://es.mongabay.com/2019/11/investigaciones-de-valeria-souza-en-cuatro-cienegas/|access-date=2021-03-09|website=Mongabay}}</ref> Her interest in biology was further cemented after she was given a ''Time Life'' book to read about the discovery of [[DNA]] when she was ten years old.<ref name=":8" />  Souza received a B.S. in biology in 1983 and a Master's degree in biology in 1985 from the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM).<ref name=":1" /> In 1990, also at UNAM, she received a Ph.D in microbial ecology from the Institute of Ecology (formerly known as the Ecology Center).<ref name=":1" /> She was a postdoctoral fellow from 1990-1992 in the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI) with [[Richard Lenski]] where she worked on the long-term [[E. coli]] experiment.<ref name=":1" /> She continued her work with Lenski for one additional year at the Center for Microbial Ecology at  [[Michigan State University]] following Lenski's move to Michigan from UCI. She is married to Dr. Luis Eguiarte, who is also a scientist.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|last=Miranda|first=Fanny|date=2019-10-29|title="Soy una figura mitológica en Cuatro Ciénegas, no saben si dragón o unicornio": Souza|url=https://www.milenio.com/ciencia-y-salud/valeria-souza-figura-mitologica-cienegas-dragon-unicornio|access-date=2021-03-09|website=Milenio}}</ref>

== Research ==
Souza has 214 major publications and has received over 8600 citations.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=O086HIwAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Google Scholar Page|access-date=2020-04-21}}</ref>  Her research focuses mainly on understanding the evolutionary, physiological, and ecological processes that are involved in the [[adaptation]], [[speciation]], and diversification of the biodiversity of [[microorganisms]]. Much of her research and conservation efforts focus on microbial mats and communities in [[Cuatro Ciénegas]], [[Coahuila]], Mexico.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Emmott|first=Robin|date=2007-02-22|title=Scientists press Mexico to protect oasis that holds biological clues|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/73036918/|access-date=2021-03-09}}</ref> The work has revealed that [[microbes]] in these [[desert]] springs represent unique microbial lineages which she has worked to study and protect from [[groundwater extraction]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://freshwater-science.org/awards-programs/environmental-stewardship|title=Environmental Stewardship Award|access-date=2020-04-21}}</ref> As a result of multiple years of work in Cuatro Ciénegas the book [https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783319934228 "Cuatro Ciénegas, Ecology, Natural History and Microbiology"] was published by Souza and her colleagues in 2018.
